Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- SSO: Okta SAML 2.0 integration for user access and groups (SCIM provisioning likely later)
- KMS: You need BYOK / HSM-backed CMKs in your AWS account (customer-managed keys)
- Logging: 7+ year retention for audit logs; ability to export raw logs/audit trails to your Splunk/SIEM; separation of access logs vs. application logs
- Network: preference for VPC peering / private endpoints; unclear on need for air-gapped on-prem at this stage
- Compliance: requirement to support PCI and internal audit requests

Quick notes on deployment modes (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to production, but limited for BYOK & some enterprise-only KMS integrations; basic private networking options (VPC egress) available
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in a dedicated pool with private networking and stronger KMS/SSO integrations — usually a good middle ground for customers wanting isolation without full private control plane
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer control (BYOK, HSM, long-term log retention/export) — recommended when procurement/security requires customer-managed keys, strict network controls, or air-gapped requirements

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether BYOK in AWS KMS (CMK) is required, or if an initial phase with Redwood-managed KMS but exported encryption keys is acceptable?
2) Confirm the Splunk export requirement (S3 export vs. direct forwarder) and retention policy specifics (7 years minimum?).
3) If possible, share a short list of stakeholders to include in the technical deep-dive (IT Sec, infra, legal).

I looped in Lauren (solutions) and Rafael (AE) — Lauren, Rafael: can you weigh in on the recommended deployment path based on the bullet points above and availability for a 60–90 min technical deep-dive this week or next?

Thanks —

Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our end: 

- SSO: Yes, Okta SAML 2.0 is required. We will want group mapping and SAML assertions for role-based access. SCIM provisioning is nice-to-have but not required for initial rollout.
- KMS/HSM: We require BYOK. Specifically, customer-managed CMKs in our AWS account backed by an HSM (we use AWS KMS with CloudHSM). We need to ensure that keys cannot be exported and that Redwood can integrate to encrypt at rest using our CMKs.
- Logging retention/export: 7 years minimum for audit logs. We need the ability to export raw logs (access + audit trails) to our Splunk instance. Ideally an S3 export that our SIEM ingests; if that's not possible we need a forwarder option.
- Network: We want private connectivity — VPC peering or PrivateLink. Air-gapped on-prem isn't required for the first deployment, but the security team will want to understand the path to a private control plane if needed later.

Can you advise which deployment mode you recommend given the above constraints? Also share any docs we should pass to procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Samir

Thanks for the forward, Marissa — reviewed Samir's notes. High level recommendation and technical constraints below.

Short answer: both Dedicated and Private can meet the requirements, but which to choose depends on admin control and procurement appetite:

Option A — Dedicated (recommended in many enterprise cases):
- Supports private networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink) and can be configured to use customer KMS keys via cross-account access and external key policies. We can integrate with AWS KMS CMKs (HSM-backed) for encrypting model weights at rest, and ensure keys never leave FintechCo's account.
- Log export: we can configure periodic S3 exports for audit logs which your SIEM can ingest. Retention policies can be applied on your S3 side for 7+ years.
- SSO: Okta SAML is supported; group mapping and SAML assertions are supported. SCIM provisioning can be added in phase 2.
- Timeline: typical Dedicated onboarding + KMS integration + network setup ~ 4–6 weeks with prioritized engineering support.

Option B — Private (VPC / private control plane):
- Provides the highest level of control (own control plane, full BYOK, closer to on-prem deployment). Best if procurement/security requires customer-managed control plane or air-gapped deployment later.
- More procurement effort and longer timeline (~8–12 weeks) and additional infra coordination (network + KMS + monitoring).

Open questions we need from FintechCo to finalize:
1) Confirm AWS account details for KMS cross-account access (account id, key ARNs) or whether they'll grant a role for Redwood to use CMKs.
2) Confirm Splunk ingestion method (S3 bucket name with permissions vs. forwarder endpoint).
3) Who is the procurement and security approver we should include in the technical workshop?

Attachments: deployment-recommendation.md (technical notes)

Suggested next step: 60–90 min technical deep-dive with Samir + IT Sec + infra + our SE team. I have availability Thu 8/6 10–12 or Mon 8/10 9–12 PT. I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.
